title: Indian Cricket Told to Prepare for Life Without Jasprit Bumrah in Test Format
excerpt: BCCI sources indicate the star pacer may be prioritised for ODIs over Tests after recurring injuries, with the 2027 World Cup taking precedence over the World Test Championship.
body:
• BCCI sources say Indian cricket may have to start preparing for life without Bumrah in longer formats after next year
  • The 32-year-old has been ruled out of the two-match Test tour of Sri Lanka due to a knee issue sustained during the ODI series against England
  • Bumrah is expected to be prioritised for the 2027 ODI World Cup over Tests and T20Is
  • Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi Dar will form India's pace attack for the Sri Lanka tour

India's cricket establishment has been warned to begin preparing for a future without pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, particularly in Test cricket, according to a BCCI source quoted by The Times of India.

"Indian cricket may have to now start getting ready for life without Bumrah especially in the longer formats after next year."

— BCCI source, via Times of India

Bumrah's latest setback — a knee injury sustained during India's recent ODI series against England — has ruled him out of the upcoming two-match Test tour of Sri Lanka. The injury adds to a growing list of fitness concerns that have plagued the fast bowler throughout his career despite his status as one of the most impactful pace bowlers in world cricket.

Centre of Excellence Taking Cautious Approach

Staff at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru are being extremely cautious regarding Bumrah's recovery. No fixed timeline has been set for the 32-year-old's return to competitive action.

https://x.com/Anurag9793/status/2087460396689129785

"The CoE was working on increasing Bumrah's workload before the Test series in Sri Lanka. It was felt that he would not be ready in time. It has been a long time since he has bowled in longer formats for a while. The CoE is very careful about him. They haven't given any timeline on him."

— BCCI source

Given the recurring nature of Bumrah's injuries, the expectation within the BCCI is that the pacer will be prioritised for ODIs rather than Tests or T20Is, with the 2027 ODI World Cup just over a year away. That tournament represents India's most high-profile short-format commitment in the near future.

Impact on World Test Championship Hopes

Bumrah's absence is likely to significantly hurt India's chances of reaching the World Test Championship 2025-27 final. The team needs a strong run of results in upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka, New Zealand and Australia to qualify.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=nb9VJZ4Uzs0

Without their most reliable pace weapon, India's bowling attack for the Sri Lanka Tests will be led by Mohammed Siraj, with Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi Dar completing the fast bowling contingent. While capable individually, the group lacks Bumrah's ability to produce breakthroughs in flat conditions.

A Broader Injury Crisis

Bumrah's situation is part of a wider fitness crisis afflicting Indian cricket. Recent reports have highlighted communication breakdowns between the Centre of Excellence and team management, with BCCI officials acknowledging that several players have been fielded before being fully fit. Captain Shubman Gill has publicly stressed the importance of workload management following India's ODI series defeat to England.

The board has yet to appoint a new head of medical staff, and Standard Operating Procedures prepared in 2023 have not been revised, raising questions about the infrastructure supporting player welfare at the highest level.

Looking Ahead

For Indian cricket fans across the diaspora, the prospect of Test cricket without Bumrah represents a significant shift. The pacer's record of 181 wickets in 40 Tests at an average of 20.07 makes him statistically India's most effective fast bowler in the format. His absence will test the depth of India's pace reserves and the team management's ability to develop viable alternatives in time for the next cycle of marquee Test assignments.
